title: City of Edmonton Point Access Block catalogue Example C
code_edition: National Building Code - 2023 Alberta Edition (printing unstated in the source)

facts.text: The catalogue matrix maps Example C to three 33-foot lots in Small Scale Residential, Small Scale Flex Residential, and Small-Medium Transition Residential Zones.
facts.locator: Point Access Block Design Guide, PDF p. 6.

facts.text: Example C labels the scenario: Small Scale: 2 floors plus basement, 8 units / 25 bedrooms, 24 cars. Small Scale Flex and Small-Medium Transition: 4 floors plus basement, 16 units / 51 bedrooms, 24 cars.
facts.locator: Point Access Block Design Guide, PDF p. 18, Example C; catalogue matrix on PDF p. 6.

facts.text: The guide says Examples A-M are inspirational general design intentions; the examples are incomplete, are not intended for development or building permit approval, and do not include information specific to a particular site.
facts.locator: Point Access Block Design Guide, PDF pp. 6-7.

facts.text: The accompanying Building Code Guide identifies NBC(AE) Division B, Part 3, Sentence 3.4.2.1.(1) (minimum number of exits) as the acceptable solution forming the basis of departure for contemplated PABs, and lists functional/objective attributions; the guide does not establish their applicability to any real proposal.
facts.locator: Point Access Block Building Code Guide, PDF p. 4.

facts.text: The Building Code Guide describes its analysis assumptions as Group C dwelling units served by the single stair, other major occupancies complying with their applicable acceptable solutions and not communicating directly with Group C, and no additional alternative solutions; confirm these conditions for any actual proposal.
facts.locator: Point Access Block Building Code Guide, PDF p. 2.

facts.text: The expanded Design Study 2 describes three consolidated 33-foot lots at a mid-block location, adaptable to two consolidated 50-foot lots; it describes a four-storey scheme in RSF or RSM Zones, adaptable in height to the RS Zone, with up to 16 units and an underground garage containing 16 stalls plus 0.5 surface stalls per unit.
facts.locator: Point Access Block Design Guide, PDF p. 11.

facts.text: The technical report uses Design Study 2 as an exemplar for a four-storey, 16-unit proposal with a vestibule and states its analysis demonstrated equivalent resilience to a two-stair design; it is a technical report conclusion, not an AHJ permit decision.
facts.locator: Point Access Block Technical Report, PDF p. 6, Executive Summary.

facts.text: The City PAB guide requires an Alternative Solution prepared by a qualified Fire Protection or Life Safety Code Consultant; it also defines professional involvement to include registered architects and/or engineers in design, field review, and Alternative Solution preparation, with plans/specifications authenticated under professional practice standards. A pre-application meeting is recommended.
facts.locator: Point Access Block Alternative Solution Guide, PDF pp. 4 and 8.

limitations: This is a documented illustrative design catalogue entry, not an individual application, issued permit, or AHJ decision.
The guide expressly says its design examples are incomplete and not for development or building-permit approval; site-specific information may be absent.

The Design Guide names the NBC(AE) 2023 edition in its companion guide, but does not identify a printing. The code-guide attribution is source content and is not independently validated against the current code.
No applicant or owner facts were added. Lot size, zone, floors, units, bedrooms, and parking are source-labeled conceptual scenario values.
The outcome-reference report analyzes Design Study 2 only; its conclusion must not be generalized to the other catalogue examples or to an unverified project.
Design Study 2 is cross-referenced to Example C by the catalogue matrix; it is an expanded view of C, not an additional case.
